recent_candidates.title: A French Impressionists undated planner, a Veuve Clicquot–inspired pencil cup, scissors from Italy, stationery from Belgium, and more upgrades to your desk with these beautifully designed items from The Reader’s Catalog
recent_candidates.excerpt: “One must from time to time attempt things that are beyond one’s capacity.” —Pierre-Auguste Renoir French Impressionists Undated Planner You can begin using this undated planner any time of year, but it’s much more than a week-by-week calendar. It has been designed with room for the lists we make in our heads late at night, space to make miscellaneous notes, room to journal, and in general a little more undesignated “elbow room” than a classic planner. There are areas for Accomplishments and Projects Completed, Projects in Process, Personal Highlights, Ideas, Notes, and Sketches, Reflections on the Past Season—all reminders that weeks and months are more than passing time. This is a lovely record of a year that can be tucked away as a keepsake. More than a dozen stunning Impressionist paintings are scattered throughout, including Claude Monet’s Bridge Over a Pond of Water Lillies and Gustave Caillebotte’s Dahlias, Garden at Petit Gennevilliers. Included are four postcards to detach and share. About two miles northeast of Jalud, in the town of Qusra, the settlers have been engaged in a monthslong campaign of bloody intimidation: On July 26 settlers burned down the al-Rahma mosque in the village. Around that time armed settlers brutally attacked Palestinian farmers from the village and the Israeli and international activists who were trying to protect them; several were severely wounded. In March twenty-eight-year-old Amir Moatasem Odeh was killed by a settler; another stabbed his father. A few weeks earlier, on February 27, settlers stormed into Qusra and nearly clubbed to death two activists who are friends of mine; a third activist managed to film the attack.
